obligation_2_case_fold.java: DiagramType#check (DiagramType.java:218-220) is String#regionMatches(true, p, key, 0, len): per UTF-16 unit, equal, or Character.toUpperCase equal, or Character.toLowerCase of those equal. findStartTypes checks 'start' the same way; getTypes switches on Character.toLowerCase of the first unit after 'start' (94-95) before its checks.
obligation_2_case_fold.rust_divergence: start_directive_type and start_type_is compare an ASCII byte prefix with eq_ignore_ascii_case, so '\startm\u0131ndmap' (dotless i) is not MINDMAP (DL q7_type_bs_dotless_mindmap).
obligation_2_case_fold.planned_change: A per-unit port of regionMatches(ignoreCase) against the ASCII keys ('start' and the getTypes keys): a text unit matches key letter k when it is k, or its Java simple uppercase or lowercase equals k's. Java's simple case mappings (Character#toUpperCase(char), #toLowerCase(char)) are UnicodeData fields 12/13; over Unicode 15.0 the non-ASCII BMP units that match an ASCII letter under that rule are exactly U+0130 (i), U+0131 (i), U+017F (s) and U+212A (k). support/gen_ascii_fold.py derives this set from UnicodeData.txt 15.0.0 (sha256 806e9aed...6a73) and a unit test pins it. No full Unicode case fold: U+00DF (sharp s) does not match 's' (its simple uppercase is itself). The switch character keeps Character.toLowerCase semantics (U+212A -> 'k', U+0130 -> 'i'; dotless i and long s stay themselves, so they never select a case).
